data.gender_notes: Sada is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word σαδαῖος (sadaios), meaning just, righteous, or religious. The name Sada carries the meaning “Righteous, Just” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sada usually hope their child will grow to embody righteous, just and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of moral purity and faithfulness.
data.etymology: Sada belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Righteous, Just.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sada total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: סדה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סדה הוא עברי ומקורו במילה 'צדקה' או 'הוגן'. הוא קשור למושגים של צדק, יושר והוגנות. בתרבות היהודית, השם סדה מייצג את הערכים הללו ומשדר אישיות ישרה והוגנת.

in_greek.name: Σάδα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σάδα στην ελληνική παράδοση σχετίζεται με τις έννοιες της δικαιοσύνης και της ευσέβειας. Στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία, το όνομα αυτό μπορεί να συμβολίζει την προσπάθεια για μια ζωή σύμφωνα με τις αρχές της δικαιοσύνης και της αρετής.

in_latin.name: Sada
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sada in traditione Latina connotationes justitiae et rectitudinis habet. In primitiva Ecclesia, hoc nomen fortasse vitam secundum justitiae et virtutis principia significabat.

in_english.name: Sada
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sada, derived from Hebrew roots, signifies righteousness, justice, and honesty. It reflects a personality characterized by integrity and fairness. Historically, the name may relate to biblical concepts of justice and righteousness, embodying Christian values of morality and virtue.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sada" showcases the rich heritage of the early Christians who adopted Greek names during the Hellenistic period. Greek culture influenced early Christianity in various ways, one of which was the naming tradition. Having a name like "Sada" speaks to the legacy of this fascinating blending of cultures and the enduring impact it continues to have on Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Sada" symbolizes a commitment to live justly, righteously, and religiously in accordance with biblical teachings. It is a reminder of the importance of being a reflection of God's love and mercy in the world -- a beacon of compassion and justice. Moreover, it encourages the bearer to strive for spiritual growth and moral excellence daily, guided by divine wisdom and Christ's example.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In ancient Mesopotamia, Sada was a goddess of fertility and prosperity. The name Sada carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Sada was associated with the Sumerian goddess of the same name, who was revered for her role in ensuring the fertility of the land and the prosperity of its people.
